negative-marking rate, a profile with no objective paper (nothing could ever be mocked), and
`verify: false` on a `patternSource` that was never fetched. Adding a profile means a `profile(...)`
entry, a loader in `src/modules/trainer/exam/data.ts`, a line in `scripts/ingest/validate_data.py`'s
`MANIFEST` and the `exam-profiles` digest in `data/_meta/versions.json` — `tests/exam-data.test.ts`
will tell you which you forgot.

`data/library/aids/*.json` is **hand-authored**, on no script and no cron: an aid is an explanation,
and the four stages that produce one are a reading job (`docs/AUTHORING.md`). It is validated like
every other dataset — `scripts/ingest/validate_data.py` (now 114 datasets) and
`tests/library-aids.test.ts`.

`node scripts/drafting-fixtures.mjs` (and `--check`) writes `tests/fixtures/drafting/*` — the ten
files the import edge-case matrix runs against. A `.docx` and a `.pdf` are opaque in a diff, so every
one is built from source in that script and the source says what it is for; the `.docx` files are
written by **the app's own zip writer** (`src/lib/drafting/zip.ts`, loaded through Vite's SSR module
runner), which exercises it against mammoth as a side effect. CI runs `--check` in the `unit` job,
so a fixture cannot drift from the source that explains it. Hand-run otherwise.

`node scripts/library-extracts.mjs` (and `--check`) writes `data/library/{definitions,quickref}/*.json`
by running the app's own parsers through Vite's SSR module runner. Hand-run, on no cron, for the
reason `pay_matrix.py` is not on one — see ADR-039 §4.

### The Tier 2 proxy

`worker/` is a **separate package** with its own dependency tree (miniflare pulls workerd, ~90 MB),
its own tsconfig and its own lockfile. `pnpm install` at the root does not touch it and `pnpm check`
does not cover it — CI does, in the `worker` job. Read `worker/README.md` before deploying; read
`docs/AI.md` §12 for the order to turn the tiers on.

````bash
cd worker && pnpm install --ignore-workspace
pnpm test          # 42: policy.test.ts by calling, worker.test.ts through real workerd
pnpm typecheck
pnpm dev           # wrangler dev
pnpm deploy        # or the workflow_dispatch-only .github/workflows/deploy-worker.yml
```                                   |

### The data pipeline

```bash
cd scripts/ingest && python3 -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install -r requirements.txt
scripts/ingest/.venv/bin/python scripts/ingest/ncrb_sankalan.py            # refresh data/law from NCRB
scripts/ingest/.venv/bin/python scripts/ingest/ncrb_sankalan.py --offline  # reparse raw/, no network

scripts/ingest/.venv/bin/python scripts/ingest/pay_matrix.py --check       # re-derive the 540 cells, write nothing
scripts/ingest/.venv/bin/python scripts/ingest/drafting_seed.py            # write data/drafting/*
scripts/ingest/.venv/bin/python scripts/ingest/drafting_seed.py --check    # rebuild and compare, write nothing

scripts/ingest/.venv/bin/python scripts/ingest/holidays.py 2026            # write data/holidays/holidays-2026.json
scripts/ingest/.venv/bin/python scripts/ingest/holidays.py 2026 --check    # rebuild and compare, write nothing
scripts/ingest/.venv/bin/python scripts/ingest/utils_seed.py               # write data/portals.json + data/pension/pension-facts.json
scripts/ingest/.venv/bin/python scripts/ingest/utils_seed.py --check       # rebuild and compare, write nothing

scripts/ingest/.venv/bin/python scripts/ingest/library_seed.py             # write data/library/* (structure only; copies no text)
scripts/ingest/.venv/bin/python scripts/ingest/library_seed.py --check     # rebuild all 16 files and compare, write nothing

scripts/ingest/.venv/bin/python scripts/ingest/validate_data.py            # every dataset vs its JSON Schema
````

### The rules-authoring pipeline

Read `docs/AUTHORING.md` before adding an act, a card kind, or a question. It is on no cron either,
for the same reason: a rule book changes when a Ministry amends it.

```bash
scripts/ingest/.venv/bin/python scripts/authoring/fetch_sources.py         # 21 documents -> sources/ (git-ignored) + SOURCES.md
scripts/ingest/.venv/bin/python scripts/authoring/extract_rules.py         # -> data/rules/text/*.json
scripts/ingest/.venv/bin/python scripts/authoring/extract_rules.py --audit-hindi   # measure each Hindi text layer
scripts/ingest/.venv/bin/python scripts/authoring/qa_pipeline.py dedup     # stage D, rapidfuzz
scripts/ingest/.venv/bin/python scripts/authoring/make_cards.py            # -> data/rules/cards/*.json + index.json
scripts/ingest/.venv/bin/python scripts/authoring/qa_pipeline.py report --date $(date +%F)

scripts/ingest/.venv/bin/python -m unittest discover -s scripts/authoring -t scripts/authoring
```

Read `scripts/ingest/README.md` before touching any of these. Three rules there are structural, not
stylistic: the weekly cron may never write to `data/law/overlays/` (a step in
`.github/workflows/ingest-law.yml` fails the run if it does); `indiacode_seed.py` may never be added
to that workflow — India Code is fetched by hand, cited, and never crawled (ADR-012); and
`pay_matrix.py` is not on any cron either, because the pay matrix changes when a Pay Commission is
implemented, not when a portal is re-published; and `drafting_seed.py` is not on one because the
Manual of Office Procedure is revised by a new **edition**, and a new edition is a reading job. It reaches no host at all: every input is in
`ANCHORS` at the top of the file, and `--check` re-derives all 540 cells and compares them against
the figures read off the gazette (ADR-016).

### The AI layer

Read `docs/AI.md` before adding a tool, adding an agent, or touching anything under `src/ai`. Four rules
are load-bearing, and each is enforced by a test rather than by convention:

1. `src/app/store.ts` may import **only** `src/ai/flags.ts`. Everything else in `src/ai` sits behind a
   dynamic import, because laziness here is a privacy property, not a performance one — a reader who
   never turns AI on never downloads the code that could reach the network
   (`tests/bundle-budget.test.ts`).
2. `src/ai/providers/wire.ts` is the **only** module allowed to call `fetch`, by a file-scoped exception
   in `eslint.config.js`. Do not reach the network as `globalThis.fetch` to get around the rule — the
   written exception is what keeps the audit question answerable from one file.
3. Every agent runs through `runAgent` with `groundedRequired`. An answer that cites no tool result, or
   that states a section or rule number no cited snippet contains, is discarded rather than shown.
4. A tool is a pure function over local data — bundled `/data` JSON or the reader's own IndexedDB rows.
   Never the network. Both `{ en, hi }` descriptions are required; a missing Hindi one throws at
   registration.

### Notes for the next session

- **A route literal and a module specifier are the same string in the same quotes, and a regex
  cannot tell them apart.** A bulk path rewrite over `src/` matched `/library` and `/utils` with a
  lookahead of ``["'`?#$]`` — which is also the closing quote of an import — so `@/lib/utils` became
  `@/lib/tools` and `@/lib/library` became `@/lib/study/read` across 117 files. `pnpm typecheck`
  caught it in under a minute and it was repaired by restoring every changed import LINE from
  `HEAD`, but the cheap lesson is the one to keep: rewrite paths through the `url.ts` helpers that
  already centralise them (`src/modules/library/url.ts` alone covered a third of this session's
  links), and read `git diff --stat` on any bulk substitution before running the tests.

- **`playwright.config.ts` has `reuseExistingServer: !CI`, and a server left listening from a
  killed run means the NEXT run never builds.** Two whole e2e runs this session were graded against
  a `dist/` that predated the fixes under test — the same failures, in the same three specs, after
  each had already been fixed. `lsof -nP -iTCP:4173` before believing a local run, and check
  `ls -la dist/index.html` against the clock. CLAUDE.md already recorded this trap; it is recorded
  again because it cost twenty minutes twice in one session.

- **Two Escape handlers on one press, again — and the fix is the CAPTURE phase.** `FocusLayout`
  leaves a focus screen on Escape and skips when a dialog is open. In the bubble phase that check is
  worthless: Radix has already handled the same press and removed its dialog from the DOM, so
  closing the editor's shortcuts sheet also threw the officer out of the document. The listener is
  `addEventListener('keydown', onKeyDown, true)` so it runs while the dialog is still there.
  ADR-029's addendum recorded the same shape for the command palette and the AI consent modal.

- **`TabLayout` owns the section's `<h1>`, and seventeen pages became `<h2>`.** A spec asserting a
  page's own title inside a section wants `{ level: 2 }`; a detail or focus page still owns its
  `<h1>`. `PageHeader`'s `as` prop is how a page says which it is, and it defaults to `h1` so the
  quiet direction is the safe one. Related: `/settings/ai`'s masthead is the SECTION's name ("AI")
  and not the feature's, because `AiSettingsSection` renders its own `<h2>` with the on/off badge —
  promoting that `<h2>` to `<h1>` instead made the page jump h1 → h3, which axe reports.

- **A "More" sheet is not the only thing that hides at level 3.** The app's top bar goes with it, and
  with it the language toggle, the theme toggle and the way to Settings. The FocusBar's ⋯ menu
  carries all three with the SAME accessible names, which is what let `setLanguage` in
  `tests/e2e/fixtures.ts` grow one branch rather than every focus-route spec growing a workaround.
  If you add a control to `TopBar`, ask whether a reader inside the reader or the editor needs it.

- **`useLiveQuery` in a section ROUTER re-renders the whole section, and that is a layout shift at
  the top of every page in it.** `DraftPage` reads the Register's follow-up count for its sub-tab
  badge; when it resolves the strip grows. It is cheap and exact, which is why that badge is the
  only one wired — Study's "due reviews" would need the 4 MB catalogue, and a count that disagrees
  with the Practise page one tap later is worse than no count.

- **A hand-written redirect table is worth more than a derived one.** `tests/redirects.test.tsx`
  lists all 38 old URLs and their targets BY HAND, because a test that reads the same array the
  code reads asserts that the array equals itself. What is worth checking is that each row goes
  where somebody's two-year-old bookmark meant to go — and a second test then fails if a row of
  `LEGACY_REDIRECTS` is missing from the hand-written list, which is the half a human forgets.

- **Deleting a page deletes every surface that page was the only mount for, and the cascade is not
  visible from the file you delete.** `EditorPage.tsx` was the only screen mounting the Rajbhasha
  glossary sheet, the phrase library and "Draft with AI". All three are still in the tree with their
  unit tests green and no route reaching them — `docs/DATA-GAPS.md` #94, deliberately a gap rather
  than a quiet deletion of three shipped features. Before removing a route, grep for what its page
  imports that nothing else does.

- **`RecentDrafts` opens a Session 8 draft by MIGRATING it first.** Letting `/draft/:type` redirect
  to `/draft/new/:type` would have created a blank document of the right type and silently discarded
  the officer's afternoon — a redirect that appears to work and throws the work away is worse than a
  dead link. `migrateOneDraft` copies, is idempotent, and leaves `drafts` untouched.

- **A data change can break a consumer that was correct when it was written, and no test will
  fail.** Reading the First Schedule's continuation rows gave BNS 77 two classification rows with
  the same clause, and `ClassificationTable` keyed its rows `key={row.clause}` — correct in every
  build before this one. React reconciles by key, and the two limbs of that section differ on
  exactly the value an officer is reading. Nothing in the suite noticed. **After changing the SHAPE
  of a dataset — not its values, its shape — grep for what consumes it and ask what each consumer
  assumed about uniqueness, ordering and arity.** `.find()` on a field that is no longer unique is
  the same defect waiting one call site over; `src/ai/tools/law.ts` was checked and maps all rows.

- **A content assertion cannot see a React key collision, and the first two tests written for that
  one passed against it.** React logs `Encountered two children with the same key` and renders both
  rows anyway, so "both limbs render" and "they show different bailability" are both green against
  the duplicate. The test that catches it spies on `console.error`. Fourth time this project has
  recorded "break the code and watch the new assertion go red before believing it" — and the first
  where the too-weak test was written _during an edge-case pass whose whole purpose was to distrust
  exactly that_.

- **A predicate reachable only through the filesystem is a predicate whose edges nobody has seen.**
  `audit_hindi`'s `usable` could only be exercised by putting a PDF on disk and naming it in the
  manifest, and it had two holes: it never gated on `devanagariRatio` despite its own docstring
  claiming three tests, so an ENGLISH document labelled `lang: "hi"` came back usable; and it had no
  minimum volume, so a scan yielding a dozen glyphs scored a perfect ratio against almost no
  denominator. Both were found by splitting `measure_hindi_layer()` out as a pure function and
  calling it with text no real document produces. Note the direction that matters: a false UNUSABLE
  costs a hand-check, a false USABLE is what would let somebody extract garbled statute.

- **A measurement that says "no" is worth a session, and the reusable part is the CONTROL rather
  than the conclusion.** Two of this session's findings are negative results, and both are now
  written where the next person will hit them. Before re-trying #58's option (b), check whether the
  route's view chunk is already named in `ROUTE_CRITICAL_MODULES` — a preload hint and a static
  import remove the same round trip, and the hint was already there. Before reading any performance
  number, check `uptime` AND ask which routes moved: a change to route splitting cannot plausibly
  move `/tools` and `/settings`, so when it appears to, the machine is the cause.

- **A test that measures a property of the CHARACTERS cannot see a font that uses the right
  characters wrongly.** `--audit-hindi` had two tests, both about which codepoints appear, and both
  are satisfied by a legacy font that maps Devanagari glyphs onto Devanagari codepoints in VISUAL
  order. It reported CSMOP's Hindi as usable while `docs/DATA-GAPS.md` #36 recorded it as
  unreadable — the audit was contradicting a finding this repository had already written down.
  `visual_order_share()` is the fix and it needs no word list, which is what makes it honest: a
  token beginning with a matra is impossible in logical-order Unicode, so no document can pass by
  using vocabulary the checker happens to know. **When an audit and a `DATA-GAPS` row disagree,
  one of them is wrong and it is worth ten minutes to find out which.**

- **Writing the control for that detector found a false positive, and the false positive was
  right.** The test asserting this project's own authored Hindi scores 0.0 failed on
  `ccs-conduct.json` — because its `_note` field QUOTES the corrupt extraction (`ूशासन` for
  `प्रशासन`) as the reason the file exists. The detector was correct and the test's scope was
  wrong; it skips `_`-prefixed metadata keys now. Same shape as `src/lib/study/purity.test.ts`
  needing to strip comments because `quiz.ts` names `Math.random()` in a comment explaining why it
  does not call it. **A checker run over a corpus that documents the thing being checked will find
  the documentation.**

- **A test that silently zeroes on a missing variable passes against the code it was written to
  catch.** The third assertion in `tests/e2e/pwa-toast.spec.ts` read `parseFloat(raw) || 0`, and
  against the pre-fix build — where neither custom property existed — that made
  `padding >= 0 + 12 + 84` true by arithmetic. It went green on exactly the defect it existed for.
  It reads `NaN` for an absent variable now and asserts on that first. Fourth time this project has
  recorded a version of "break the code and watch the new assertion go red before believing it";
  the other three are `network.sentinel`, the law-search heading probe, and Session 30's three
  proxy assertions.

- **`data/pension/` had no dataset test of any kind, and nothing found that until a row was
  closed.** `src/lib/pension/engine.test.ts` is thorough and runs entirely against a FIXTURE, so
  the committed table it is modelling was read by nothing. `tests/pension-data.test.ts` is the
  missing half. Worth a sweep: a `data/` directory whose only tests are engine tests over fixtures
  is a directory where a corrupted number reaches the reader.

- **A parser that reads "the rows that have an identifier" will silently drop the rows that
  continue them.** `parse_first_schedule` read only Schedule rows carrying a section number, and 25
  rows continue the row above with an empty section column. The failure is invisible in every
  aggregate — 288 sections classified, 288 expected — and shows up only as a legally wrong answer
  on individual sections: BNS 77 and 78(2) are bailable on a first conviction and non-bailable on a
  second, and only the first row was read. **When a table has a column that can be blank, ask what
  a blank MEANS there before filtering on it.**

- **`git add -A` in a shared working tree sweeps up your peer's uncommitted work, and the commit then
  tells a story that is not true.** It happened this session: commit `9613b67`, whose subject is an
  exam-mode edge pass, also carries a concurrent session's BNSS First Schedule parser fix, four
  regenerated `data/law` datasets, a service-worker toast fix and two new test files. Nothing was
  lost and the peer caught it within minutes, but a reader bisecting later would have found a First
  Schedule fix inside an exam commit with no explanation. The tip had nothing on top of it so the
  MESSAGE was amended to list what the commit actually carries — history was not rewritten, because
  re-splitting two sessions' trees mid-flight is a worse trade than an accurate note. **`git add
<paths>`, and `git diff --cached --stat` before every commit.** Two seconds.

- **A contended machine produces Lighthouse numbers that look exactly like a regression.** A peer's
  first run this session came back 5–15 points down on every route while a 5,500-test suite was
  running next to it (load average 41). The tell was that `/tools` and `/settings` dropped too, which
  the change under test could not plausibly affect — so the common cause was the machine. Check the
  load average before reading a performance number, and ask which routes moved: a change that only
  touches route splitting cannot move a route it does not touch. CLAUDE.md already records the
  neighbouring version of this, where a concurrent `pnpm build` replaced `dist/` mid-run.

- **An edge-case pass over this session found THIRTEEN defects, and eleven were the app not trusting
  its own storage or its own call sites.** ADR-044's addendum has all thirteen;
  `src/lib/exam/edge.test.ts` and `src/modules/trainer/exam/edge.test.tsx` are the regression files,
  and every test in them was confirmed to fail against the committed code first. There is no model in
  this module, so the ADR-032/ADR-035 conclusion ("the model's half was guarded and the code's half
  was not") does not apply — the DATA was guarded here, and what was not was **a row out of IndexedDB
  and this session's own callers.** The four most transferable are below.

- **A function that cannot read its input has to say so, not return a plausible number.** `daysUntil`
  walked `addIstDays` to a five-year limit and returned the limit, so a date ten years out reported
  1,830 days — and so did a string that is not a date at all. A corrupt row and a real long window
  were literally the same value. It returns `null` for anything that is not an IST calendar day now,
  and computes the rest exactly; `buildPlan` distinguishes `unreadableDate` from `expired` for the
  same reason, having previously drawn four hundred days for a date that is not a date, because
  `'not-a-day' < '2026-09-04'` is false as a string comparison.

- **THREE branches were reachable in the library and dead from the only place that calls them**, which
  makes it five times this project has hit that family. `take-mock` had its kind, its i18n key and its
  slot — and the hub passed `elapsedFraction: null` on every render. Worse, `dailyBudget` reads the
  Session 28 study goals and the plan screen never passed any, **while the card underneath still read
  "Taken from your weekly Library goal"**: not a hidden branch but a false sentence on the screen. The
  repair that generalises is the one `nextActions` took — if the caller can only pass a value the
  function could compute itself, the function should compute it.

- **The caller sweep is worth nothing until it excludes tests.** Every export in this module had a
  caller on the first pass; narrowing it to PRODUCTION callers found five more, four of them real —
  a duplicated `reduce`, two store accessors nobody read, and `forgetExam`, which existed because
  "Stop preparing" ought to delete the row and instead only cleared a flag, leaving a record of which
  departmental examination an officer was preparing for. Run it as
  `grep -rln "\bNAME\b" src tests | grep -v '\.test\.'`.

- **A `verify: false` claim, a `t()` key and a control's label are all promises, and the sweeps check
  two of the three.** The i18n sweep found seven keys naming features this session did not build, and
  removing them is the right move rather than keeping one "for later" — that is how the list of
  thirty-three ADR-041's check found came to exist. Nothing mechanical catches the third: Settings'
  "Stop preparing" did something narrower than its label, and only reading the label against the
  handler finds that.

- **The boundary was the deliverable, and the concrete test of it was refusing to ship half the
  brief.** Six exam profiles were asked for; three had a fetched, gazette-notified pattern and three
  did not, and the three that did not are in `docs/DATA-GAPS.md` #91 rather than in `data/exams`.
  Read ADR-044 §1 before adding a fourth. The Income Tax one is the tempting case — the Departmental
  Examination Rules 2026 genuinely exist and a search summary quotes real figures out of them — and
  it is still a claim with no artefact behind it, because `incometaxindia.gov.in` returned 403 to
  `WebFetch` and to `curl` with a browser User-Agent alike. **A pattern transcribed from a search
  engine's summary of a document this repository never read is not a sourced pattern.**

- **A profile's NAME has to carry the CADRE, and a real reader is what found that.** An officer about
  to join the Intelligence Bureau as an ACIO said so mid-session and read `ib-so-ldce` as their
  examination. It is not: the notification's eligibility column for Category VIII names the Assistant
  and Stenographer grades — the ministerial cadre — and the executive line is a different progression
  it says nothing about. The eligibility note had said so all along, three taps down, which is not
  where anybody checks whether an examination is theirs. Any future profile whose organisation runs
  more than one cadre owes its name the same treatment. `docs/DATA-GAPS.md` #92 has what was searched.

- **"Enabling a rule book because of somebody's job is a guess about their work; putting it on a
  syllabus is a claim about an examination."** The brief suggested OSA for the IB profile, and
  `actHints.ts` already switches OSA cards on for an IB officer. It is not in the notification's
  reference list for Category VIII, so it is not a unit, and `test_exams_seed.py` asserts no profile
  maps `osa` at all. Only the second of those two claims needed a source, and that is the sentence to
  reach for the next time a plausible-sounding addition has no document behind it.

- **A figure over only what the app covers is a figure about a smaller examination.**
  `coverage.ts#mappedMarksShare` exists so the readiness number can be honest, and `ExamHubPage`
  renders it on the SAME card — a caveat one card away is a caveat nobody reads. For `css-so-ldce` it
  is exactly 0.3, and `tests/exam-data.test.ts` asserts that to ten places rather than bounding it,
  because the exact figure is the headline rather than a detail. `railway-so-ldce` is the expensive
  case the boundary produces on purpose: two mapped units against eleven, shown on the picker card
  BEFORE the reader chooses.

- **Two lists in the readiness screen were `<dl>`s and axe failed both `serious`.** `dt` and `dd`
  have to be children of the `dl` (or of one `div` under it); mine were grandchildren, inside a flex
  wrapper. Flattening the markup to satisfy the rule would have cost the layout, and the pairing was
  buying nothing the bar's own `aria-label` did not already say — so the `dl` went and a plain list
  replaced it. Only `pnpm exec playwright test` found this; the jsdom render was silent.

- **The mock defaulted to a paper this app can barely fill.** `ib-so-ldce`'s Paper I maps one of its
  five topics, so "the first objective paper" offered a fifteen-question mock that drew three —
  correct, honest, and a poor first impression of a feature whose Paper II maps eight of ten. The
  default is now the objective paper with the most MAPPED weight. Found by a browser run, because the
  jsdom test had asserted the shortfall notice rather than walking the paper.

- **Three Playwright failures in one file were the same trap: a string `name` is a case-insensitive
  SUBSTRING.** "Today" matched "today's schedule"; "Next" matched "Go to the next marked question";
  "1, blank" matched "11, blank" and "21, blank". CLAUDE.md already records this costing half an hour
  on `{ name: 'Post' }` matching "Place of posting" — this is the fourth, fifth and sixth time. Reach
  for `exact: true` first in any file with an answer sheet in it.

- **The Pixel 7 caught the Dexie-write race again.** Choosing a profile and then immediately
  `page.goto`-ing the checklist passed on the desktop and failed on mobile, reporting "the checklist
  wants an examination" — two screens from the real cause. Wait on the app's own confirmation, which
  here is the banner; CLAUDE.md records the identical shape costing the Library's annotations spec.

- **A screen with no `<h1>` while it loads is a screen a reader tabbing in cannot place, and all four
  exam routes shipped that way for an hour.** Every loading and error branch returned a bare
  `<Skeleton />`, so the route had no level-1 heading until the dataset and the Dexie row had both
  resolved. `tests/e2e/a11y.spec.ts` is what found it, and it found it as "element(s) not found"
  rather than as a slow wait — which reads exactly like contention and is not. The title is known
  before the data is, so the header goes first in every branch; that is what every other page in this
  app already does.

- **One readiness wait in the a11y sweep had been budgeted around rather than fixed.** Its own comment
  named "a 5s `expect` timeout on whichever route happened to be loading when another worker took the
  CPU" as the failure mode, and three of the four waits in that loop carry `timeout: 30_000` while the
  combobox one did not. The sweep is 45 routes now, up from the 21 its four-minute budget was written
  for — raised to five and the count corrected in the same pass. When a comment describes a flake,
  check whether the line it describes was ever actually changed.

- **`t()` is typed against the catalogue, so a template-literal key does not compile — and that is the
  feature.** `ACTION_KEYS` and `ITEM_LABELS` are literal maps from a `NextActionKind` or a checklist
  item id to a WHOLE i18n key, `satisfies Record<Kind, string>`, so a kind added to `readiness.ts`
  without a sentence beside it is a compile error rather than a row rendering its own key. The same
  shape `AiDraftPanel.tsx` uses for its per-tool labels.

- **`src/lib/exam` holds no reader-facing copy, and `purity.test.ts` asserts it by looking for a
  Devanagari code point.** The library is pure and has no `useT`, so any sentence written into it
  would be single-language by construction — the one thing the master context forbids outright. The
  exam-day checklist and the next-three-actions are therefore ids and parameters here, and sentences
  in `src/i18n`.

- **`useAsync` is now exported from `src/modules/trainer/useCatalogue.ts`.** `exam/useExam.ts` is the
  SAME module one directory down, so a second copy would have been two implementations of one hook
  rather than the per-module ownership that file's own comment argues for. The per-module rule holds
  across modules; it never meant per-directory.

- **`ExamModeSection` in Settings dynamic-imports `clearActiveExam` inside the handler and reads
  `db.examChoices` directly.** Settings is on the initial route's chunk graph, and a static import of
  `@/lib/exam` for one line would put the plan, the mock builder and the readiness engine on every
  reader's device — including everyone who never opens `/study/exam`. The initial route measures
  146.7 KB gzip against a 250 KB budget, up 0.8 from the i18n keys, and the build log carries no
  `INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT`.

- **Session 32 ran concurrently with Session 31 in this working tree and coordinated by direct
  message**, the arrangement Sessions 12/13, 14, 15, 21, 29/30 and 30/31 established. Ownership was
  split by path: Session 31 owned `src/lib/drafting/**`, `src/modules/drafting/**` and the `draft.*`
  i18n block; this one owned `src/lib/exam/**`, `src/schemas/exam.ts`,
  `src/modules/trainer/exam/**`, `data/exams/**` and `scripts/ingest/exams_seed.py`. Two things worth
  expecting: **a Dexie version has to be claimed out loud** — v16 was theirs, this session took v17
  after being told, and a `src/lib/exam/types.ts` type-import of `ExamChoiceRow` from `@/db` held
  their typecheck red until the table landed, which is a peer blocked by a file they correctly would
  not edit. And `docs/COVERAGE.md` was deliberately left stale by their commit rather than
  regenerated with an untested `src/lib/exam` in the tree — CI diffs that file, so it is regenerated
  in the commit that lands the tests.

- **An edge-case pass over this session found SEVEN defects, and they split into two families with
  different mechanical checks.** ADR-043's second addendum has all seven;
  `src/modules/drafting/{edge.test.tsx,hooks.edge.test.tsx}` and `src/lib/drafting/intake.test.ts`
  are the regression files, and every test in them was confirmed to fail against the committed code
  first.

  **Family one: state not keyed on what it is about.** The register's edit form held its draft in
  `useState(entry)` — which runs on MOUNT — so pressing Edit on a second row while the form was open
  kept the FIRST row's values and Save wrote them to the second row's id. Nothing throws and nothing
  looks wrong; the officer's correction lands on a communication they were not looking at. That is
  CLAUDE.md's own `FeynmanBox` lesson in a module that did not exist when it was written. The check
  is: **any component that edits or records something has to be keyed on the thing, and a `key` is
  the fix, never an effect that resynchronises.**

  **Family two: a fallback that quietly answers a question nobody asked.** `activeText` was
  `text || stored?.text || ''`, so Clear refilled the box from the stored letter and appeared to do
  nothing on every letter an officer comes back to — an empty string is a VALUE and `||` cannot tell
  it from an absence. And the reply form's select opened on an empty "Suggested" placeholder whose
  fallback was `templates[0]?.id`, which sorts to `acknowledgement`: every officer taking the
  default got an Acknowledgement. The check is: **a control whose value is empty is a control whose
  behaviour is decided somewhere the officer cannot see.**

- **A comment that asserts something is true elsewhere is a claim to go and check.**
  `IntakeAiPanel`'s own header said "the `key` on this component in `ReplyPage` is the letter's
  text, so pasting a second letter asks again". There was no key, so the confirmation that letter A
  could be sent silently covered letter B. Third time in four sessions — ADR-037's addendum
  (`ensureLocalEngine`'s "has to wait"), ADR-041 §2 (a purity test described before it existed), and
  now this. **Open the place a comment points at.**

- **`\b` is not the only trap with two language halves; so is WHERE the Act name sits.** `ACT_TAIL`
  read the Act after a citation, because that is where English puts it — "section 420 of the Indian
  Penal Code". Hindi puts it first: "भारतीय दंड संहिता की धारा 420". So every Devanagari citation
  came back with no Act and could never be resolved, while every English one worked. The English
  half working is not evidence (ADR-035, ADR-039, and now ADR-043). `ACT_LEAD` looks backwards and
  may not cross a sentence boundary, which is the whole risk of looking backwards.

- **A cap on the input is not a cap on what is derived from it.** The letter body is capped at
  `LETTER_CAP` characters before it is sent; `findAsks` had no cap, and every ask goes into the
  prompt — so a long circular could push a far larger context than the letter it came from.
  `MAX_ASKS` is 12, and a dropped ask carrying a DEADLINE displaces a kept one that does not,
  because a cap that silently dropped the one sentence a follow-up can be set from is worse than no
  cap. Writing that test found a third thing: "The reply may be sent by 30.09.2026" was not an ask
  at all, because it uses no request formula. **A sentence that sets a time limit is a request.**

- **Two of that pass's own tests could not fail, and were rewritten before they were believed.** One
  asserted `expect(vi.fn()).not.toHaveBeenCalled()` on a mock nothing could ever call — it passes
  against a hook with no cleanup at all. It watches the `AbortSignal` the provider was handed now,
  which is what `wire.ts` gives `fetch` and so what decides whether the officer goes on paying. The
  other polled a fixed `setTimeout(0)` for a run that needs tens of milliseconds to dynamic-import
  its agent, and reported an empty list — which looks exactly like a hook that never calls its
  provider. `ai-local.spec.ts` records the same lesson from the other end: **poll the thing you are
  asserting about, not a proxy for it.**

- **A stub of a dataset type is a stub of every field the code happens to read.**
  `{ id, checklist: [] } as unknown as DocTemplate` made `buildInstruction` throw on
  `template.layout.en`, the hook caught it, and the test failed with "the run never reached the
  provider" — which reads as a broken hook. The real committed template is one `readFileSync` away
  and cannot lie.

- **Fourth session in a row to find something wired end to end that nothing called, and this one
  slipped past the check that was invented for it.** `recordIssuedNumber` was written, tested against
  `fake-indexeddb` five ways, and called by no line of application code — the register would have
  shown inbound letters and never a single outbound communication. ADR-041's mechanical sweep (i18n
  keys no source file references) does NOT catch it, because every key involved WAS referenced, by a
  store function nobody called. The check that does catch it takes a minute: **for each function a
  session exports, name the line that makes it run.** A store function with no caller is a feature
  with no reader, one layer down from a key with no reader.

  **The same check caught a second one in the same session, and that one was a whole feature.**
  `ModifyPanel` took the scoped selection as a PROP, `DocEditorPage` never passed one, and the
  control that turned scoping on was guarded by `selection && selection.size > 0` — so
  `restrictToBlocks`, enforced in code and tested five ways in `src/ai/agents/modify.test.ts`, could
  not fire from the screen at all. What found it was working down the brief's own list at the end
  and naming, for each item, the control that makes it happen. The scope is a `<select>` of the
  document's own paragraphs now, which is also better than the editor's caret would have been: it
  keeps this panel from knowing about Tiptap, it does not change under the officer while they type
  the instruction, and it is something they can read before spending anything.

- **`INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT` in the build log is load-bearing and nobody reads build logs.**
  `ModifyPanel` imported `QUICK_ACTIONS` — one object of seven strings — statically from
  `@/ai/agents/modify`, which cancelled `useModifyAi`'s dynamic import of the same module. That
  would have put the agent, `renderDoc`, `checklist`, `proposal`, `instructions` and zod into the
  editor's chunk for every reader with AI off, and `docs/AI.md` is explicit that laziness in
  `src/ai` is a PRIVACY property rather than a performance one. `src/ai/agents/modify-actions.ts` is
  the values-only module that fixes it: **types are erased and may still be imported from a lazily
  loaded agent; values may not.** It happened TWICE in one session — the second time when the scope
  control needed `numberedBlocks`, which moved out of the agent and into
  `src/lib/drafting/proposal.ts` for the same reason. Grep the build output for that warning at the
  end of any session that adds a panel.

- **Two dates from two sources compare wrong, and it has two faces.** An intake's date is
  `2026-08-12` (read off a letter) and a document's `meta.date` is `12.08.2026` (what CSMOP prints).
  Compared as strings `04.09.2026 < 2026-08-12`, so the register sorted a September reply above the
  August letter it answered. Session 30 found the same hazard PRINTING rather than sorting — an
  exported `.docx` carrying `2026-09-03` at its head and `03.09.2026` in its body. Both fixes go
  through `format.ts` (`isoDateValue` for storage, `formatDate` for display), which is the engine's
  own reading of a date and reads both shapes in either script. Anything that takes a date from more
  than one source owes itself one of the two.

- **A letter pasted into the reply screen is stored NOWHERE until the officer keeps it**, and that
  is asserted through the real IndexedDB rather than stated. `tests/e2e/draft-reply.spec.ts` opens
  `sahayak`, counts `intakes` and expects zero after a letter has been pasted, read and left. A
  privacy claim nobody tests is a privacy claim.

- **Assertions on the reply screen must be scoped to the "What was read" region.** Every value on
  that card also exists verbatim on the page, because the letter is still in the textarea above it —
  so an unscoped `getByText` matches twice and fails on strict mode. The register's list needs the
  same treatment, because its filter `<select>`s carry "Received", "Sent" and "Pending" as hidden
  `<option>`s. Both got a NAMED region, which is the a11y fix as much as the test fix: a screen
  reader hearing the same file number twice with nothing between them cannot tell which is what the
  app read and which is the paper. CLAUDE.md already records the same shape for a study aid quoting
  the provision it explains.

- **`?? []` on a `useLiveQuery` defeats every `useMemo` below it.** A fresh array literal per render
  is a new reference, so the draft library's body search would have re-walked every document on every
  keystroke anywhere in the tree. One frozen module constant makes "still loading" and "loaded and
  empty" the same stable value. `react-hooks/exhaustive-deps` says so as a warning, which is exactly
  quiet enough to ignore.

- **The modify rationale may not name a paragraph number, and the reason worth remembering is not
  the validator.** Paragraph numbers are generated by POSITION, so a proposal is a set of controls
  that renumber the document as they are accepted — a rationale saying "paragraph 3 has been made
  firmer" is about a different paragraph by the time the officer has taken the change above it.
  (It would also fail the run, because `NUMBERED_PROVISION_PATTERN` reads `paragraph N` as a claim
  about a provision. `modify.test.ts` asserts that failure so it has a name.)

- **A partially accepted paragraph loses its marks, and the code says so rather than doing it
  quietly.** Accepting a block whole takes the model's node, marks and all; accepting some of its
  words assembles text from two different nodes and there is no honest way to decide which set of
  bold runs survives. `applyProposal` reports it in `flattened` and the panel shows a sentence. The
  alternative — keeping the before-node's marks over after-text — applies emphasis to words the
  officer never saw emphasised.

- **`lintDocument`'s glossary argument finally has a caller, and it is still not passed.** CLAUDE.md
  recorded that the terminology check "was implemented, tested five ways, and returned `[]` on every
  run" because nobody handed it `data/glossary.json`. The Change tab's "Check consistency" is the
  caller it was owed — and it deliberately passes NO glossary, because the terminology rule is the
  only one of the eight that needs 970 KB and that is not a fair price for a button. The other seven
  run. If the terminology check is ever wanted here, it wants its own lazy load and its own control,
  not a widening of this one.

- **Sessions 30 and 31 ran concurrently in this working tree and coordinated by direct message** —
  the arrangement Sessions 12/13, 14, 15, 21, 29/30 and the law/pay sessions established. Ownership
  was split by path: Session 30 owned the import/export layer and Dexie v15, this one owned
  `src/lib/drafting/{instructions,intake,proposal,register}.ts`, `src/ai/agents/{intake,modify}.ts`,
  `src/modules/drafting/{intake,register}/**` and Dexie **v16**. Four files were edited across the
  line and each was announced first: `DraftPage.tsx` (three routes above the `:type` catch-all),
  `PickerPage.tsx` (a `<DraftHome />` above their `RecentDrafts`), `DocEditorPage.tsx` (one tab, the
  register's automatic entry, and the duplicate check's second half), and
  `src/lib/drafting/purity.test.ts`, whose ledger both sessions append to. Because both had edited
  `src/i18n/*.json`, `src/db/index.ts`, `src/ai/{models,prompts}.ts` and `docs/*`, those shared files
  landed in whichever commit went first rather than being split by hunk — which is why Session 31's
  Dexie v16 and its two agent ids are in commit `66044f8` with tables and personas that nothing
  referenced yet. That is the pattern v2 and v11 already established and it is fine; what is not
  fine is splitting a 1,178-line JSON diff by hunk.

- **When a shared JSON catalogue is edited by two sessions, do not sort it.** Re-serialising
  `src/i18n/en.json` with sorted keys produced a semantically identical 1,178-line diff with 220
  real lines inside it — a diff nobody can review, and the same mistake CLAUDE.md records for
  `data/_meta/versions.json`. Rebuild the file in HEAD's key order with new keys appended in place;
  `git diff --stat` on a catalogue should be roughly the number of keys you added.

- **An edge-case pass over Session 30 found TWELVE defects, and the pattern is one sentence: the FILE
  was distrusted and the CONVERSION was not.** Every way an officer can hand this app the wrong thing
  — a `.doc` in disguise, a scan, an encrypted PDF, a garbled text layer, an over-cap file, a
  zero-byte one — already had its own refusal and a message saying what to do next, because a file is
  obviously untrusted. What failed was everything downstream of "the file is fine". ADR-042's second
  addendum has all eleven; the four most transferable are below, and every regression test was
  confirmed to fail against the committed code first.

- **A proxy assertion is not an assertion, and three of the eleven had one.** A test that the print
  route's stylesheet CHANGED, rather than that it applied. A test that numbering EXISTED, rather than
  at what level. A test that a subject CONTAINED a phrase, rather than that it ended. All three
  passed against the broken code. Before believing a new assertion here, break the code and watch it
  go red — `network.sentinel()` has the same story (ADR-031) and this is its third repetition.

- **`position: fixed` in paged media is positioned against the page's CONTENT area, not the sheet.**
  So `top: 0` on a running header is the top of the TEXT COLUMN: the letterhead printed on the
  document's first block and the page number on its last. Both bands live in the page margin now
  (`top: -20mm`, `bottom: -14mm`), and `LETTERHEAD_MAX_HEIGHT_MM` is 16mm rather than 30mm because
  that is what a 25.4mm margin holds. Any future running element owes itself the same arithmetic.

- **A nested named `@page` beats the one on its ancestor, and that is how a control comes to do
  nothing.** `A4Preview` renders `.a4-print-root`, which `index.css` pins to `page: draft-a4`. The
  print route wraps it, so the generated rule sat on the outside and Letter rewrote a stylesheet
  nothing applied. `pageRuleCss` names both selectors now, scoped under `.draft-print-root` so the
  editor's preview and every other surface sharing the class are untouched.

- **Creating a `blob:` URL during render and revoking it in an effect gives you a revoked URL on
  screen, in every `pnpm dev` session, and NO browser run in this project can see it.** StrictMode
  mounts, runs the effect, DESTROYS it and runs it again — the destroy revokes the URL while it is
  still in state and still rendered, and the recreated effect has nothing to do. Measured:
  `created: 1, src: "blob:u1", revoked: ["blob:u1"]`. `pnpm test:e2e` builds for production where
  StrictMode is inert, which is exactly the trap CLAUDE.md already records costing Session 8 two
  defects in `useDraft`. `useObjectUrl` writes the `src` on to the element in an effect and takes it
  off in the same cleanup: the DOM is an external system, which is the one thing an effect is for.

- **`'2. '.split('.')` has length TWO**, because a paragraph marker ends in a full stop and a space.
  `length - 1` put every ordinary numbered paragraph at Word level 1 and every sub-paragraph at
  level 2 — so an O.M. that should read `2.` `3.` `4.` down the left margin opened indented and
  numbered `2.1` `2.2` `2.3`. Count the GROUPS (`markerDepth` in `docx.ts`), and clamp: a reference
  to a level `numberingConfig` never defined opens unnumbered.

- **`\p{Extended_Pictographic}` includes `©`, `®` and `™`.** Stripping emoji from an export took all
  three out of every document, so a footer reading `© 2026 Government of India` exported as
  ` 2026 Government of India`. `\p{Emoji_Presentation}` is the property that actually predicts a
  black box on an office laser, and none of the three has it. `✓` survives; `✓️` loses only its
  variation selector.

- **`navigator.share` needs the transient activation of the gesture that started it, and every
  `await` on the way there spends it.** The batch builds its archive first, so a real browser rejects
  with `NotAllowedError` on a perfectly ordinary press. Swallowing every rejection as "the officer
  cancelled" left them with no file, no message and no error. A cancellation is `AbortError`;
  anything else falls back to the download and says so.

- **A subtractive test needs a floor.** "Take away the words a page number is made of and the digits,
  and if nothing is left that is all it was" drops `011-23092345` — a footer holding nothing but the
  office telephone. A line with no page WORD in it is a page number only if it is short.

- **Two dates from two sources in one place is a shape worth recognising.** A document created by the
  importer stores `2026-09-03` (a date input needs it); one typed in the Session 8 editor stores
  `03.09.2026` (CSMOP prints it). The `.docx` number/date table passed `meta.date` through untouched,
  so one sheet carried both forms — and the ISO one reached a signed document. Everything that
  displays a date goes through `format.ts#formatDate`, and everything that COMPARES two must go
  through `isoDateValue` first: the concurrent session found the same hazard sorting a register,
  where `'04.09.2026' < '2026-08-12'` as strings put a September reply above the August letter it
  answered. CLAUDE.md's own `Number(date.slice(0, 4))` trap, twice more.

- **The export panel's language selector chose between two identical files.** `DocEditorPage` renders
  `single` in the APP language and `bilingual` in both, and `documentsFor` answered `'hi'` with
  `single` — so an officer working in English who picked हिंदी got the English document under a file
  name ending `(HI)`. When two renders exist, the pair is authoritative and the single one is only a
  fallback.

- **A conversion that cannot be exact must be able to say so, and the saying has to come BEFORE the
  save.** `ImportNotice` is a code, a count and up to twelve named examples, produced by the pure
  mapping layer rather than by the screen, and the import review step lists every one under "What was
  not imported" while the officer can still go back to Word. This is `resolveAnchor`'s rule
  (ADR-039 §1) in a new place. An importer that quietly drops an image is worse than one that refuses
  the file, because the officer signs what came out.

- **mammoth accepts every tracked insertion and drops every deletion, silently — which is right, and
  is exactly why the officer must be told.** The document they are now editing is not the document
  they were sent. `scanDocumentXml` counts `w:ins`/`w:del` out of `word/document.xml`, which is also
  where merged cells and section columns are visible and in the HTML they are not. Headers and
  footers mammoth does not read AT ALL, and they are the part this app has a field for — they are
  offered for review and never applied, because a header may be a page number, a confidentiality
  stamp or a letterhead and only the officer knows which.

- **`extract.ts` is written now because Session 31 reuses it.** The register of inbound paper has to
  read the same four facts off a letter, and two extractors that disagree about what "the number" is
  would make a thread that never joins up. One grammar, one implementation — ADR-039 §4's rule, third
  application. It never invents: a field it cannot find comes back empty with `confidence: 'none'`,
  and one found without a label comes back `low` so the screen can say "please check".

- **A guard that asks "does a date appear in this" instead of "is this entirely a date" throws away
  half the file numbers in this corpus.** `12/05/2026` is a date; `12/2/2023-JCA` CONTAINS one and is
  a file number, and that is how a great many of the orders this app cites are numbered.
  `isOnlyADate` compares the match against the whole candidate. The test that caught it was written
  to check something else, which is the usual way.

- **Two columns share their baselines, so a gutter search over LINES finds nothing on exactly the
  pages it exists for.** `linesOf` groups by baseline, as it must, and therefore merges "left column
  line one" and "right column line one" into one line spanning the page. `findGutter` reads the
  ITEMS, with a `SPANNING_ALLOWANCE` of 2 so a title across the top does not defeat it — a strict
  "nothing crosses the band" test refuses most real two-column documents, because most have a title.

- **A refusal has to point at something that exists.** The export gate's blocked card said "open the
  checklist to see which" and offered no control to do it — the "wired up and cannot fire" family
  (ADR-039's second addendum) in a surface written that hour. The browser run found it, because the
  export button was simply disabled with nowhere to go. Ask what an officer does NEXT after every
  sentence that tells them something is wrong.

- **`name.slice(name.lastIndexOf('.'))` returns the last CHARACTER when there is no dot.** `README`
  had extension `"E"`. The refusal was right by accident and the message was not. Found by a browser
  run — Playwright saves a download to a temporary path with no extension — which is a browser
  finding a string-handling bug, not where anyone would look for one. The same expression is in
  `src/modules/library/personal/extract.ts` and has the same latent behaviour.

- **There is no PDF writer in this app and there should not be one.** jsPDF and pdf-lib map code
  points to glyph ids one at a time; Devanagari needs reordering, conjunct substitution and mark
  positioning, which is a HarfBuzz job neither carries. The output is `काय्रालय` where the document
  says `कार्यालय`, in a file an officer signs. The browser's own print pipeline already does it
  correctly with the fonts this app ships, so "Export PDF" is `window.print()` and a bilingual
  instruction sheet. ADR-042 §5.

- **`@page { size: var(--x) }` is invalid CSS in every browser and falls back to the printer's
  default**, which is Letter in some locales. A paper size the officer CHOSE cannot travel through a
  custom property, so `print.ts#pageRuleCss` builds the rule as literal text and `PrintPage` injects
  it in a `<style>`. It is a NAMED page, for the reason `draft-a4` and `library-a4` are named.

- **`position: fixed` inside `@media print` is how CSS 2.1 makes a running header**, and
  `counter(page)`/`counter(pages)` are the only way to know the page number. `counter(pages)` is
  unimplemented in some engines, so the word "of" is a real text node rather than generated content —
  where the total is missing the sentence still reads.

- **The letterhead IMAGE goes in the running header and the letterhead LINES do not.**
  `renderOfficialDoc`'s `applyStationery` already prepends the lines to the first `header` block, so
  passing them to the running header as well printed the officer's letterhead twice on page one. An
  image cannot travel the block path, and a repeating image is right anyway: it is the mark at the
  top of every sheet, while a letterhead is the address at the head of the first.

- **This app supplies no emblem, crest or seal and must not start.** Reproducing the State Emblem is
  governed by the State Emblem of India (Prohibition of Improper Use) Act 2005. The officer supplies
  an image their own office permits, and the card says so above the control. An uploaded SVG is never
  rendered inline — it goes in an `<img src="blob:">` where scripts do not run — and `svgIsInert` is
  the second belt so the refusal happens at upload time, where the officer can be told why.

- **`fflate` was considered and not added.** `CompressionStream`/`DecompressionStream` are native in
  every browser this app supports and in Node 18+, a `.docx` is already compressed so `STORE` is a
  real fallback rather than a compromise, and what is left of a ZIP is a container format that fits
  in a page. `src/lib/drafting/zip.ts` takes its clock as an ARGUMENT — the directory forbids one, and
  an archive that is a function of its inputs is one a test can byte-compare. Read through the
  CENTRAL DIRECTORY, never local headers from the front: a local header may defer its sizes to a data
  descriptor after the payload, and Word writes `.docx` files both ways.

- **mammoth ships two builds and Vitest resolves the OTHER one.** The browser build — what Vite
  resolves through the package's `browser` field, and therefore what ships — reads `arrayBuffer` and
  nothing else; the Node build reads `path`/`buffer`/`file` and rejects an options object carrying
  only `arrayBuffer`. `readFile.ts` passes BOTH keys, so the SHIPPED code path is what the tests
  exercise. The alternative was a test driving a different function than production does.

- **pdf.js's `workerSrc` is set only when it is unset, and that is what makes the PDF path testable
  at all.** `new URL('pdfjs-dist/build/pdf.worker.min.mjs', import.meta.url)` is the form Vite
  rewrites into a hashed same-origin asset and the only form the CSP permits — and under jsdom the
  same expression resolves to `http://localhost/...`, which pdf.js's fake-worker fallback refuses
  ("Only URLs with a scheme in: file and data are supported"). `tests/drafting-io.test.ts` points it
  at the file on disk in a `beforeAll`.

- **`Blob.prototype.stream` does not exist in jsdom**, so `readBytes` falls back to `arrayBuffer()`
  when it is absent. That is not a test accommodation: it is the same read without the early abort,
  still behind the size check, and the only thing lost is the ability to stop halfway through a file
  that lied about `size`.

- **With Word numbering ON — the default — a body paragraph's marker is not text any more.** That is
  the trade the brief asked for ("so Word renumbers on edit") and it means a re-import sees a plain
  paragraph. `tests/drafting-io.test.ts` asserts BOTH settings so the trade cannot be forgotten, and
  the numbering's `start` is taken from the marker the engine generated, so an O.M. that numbers from
  2 exports numbering that starts at 2 rather than renumbering itself the moment it opens.

- **`meta.signature` needs a telephone and an e-mail and `MetaPanel` did not offer them.**
  `checklist.ts`'s `signature-block` rule is a `must` on most forms, `meta.signature` is a snapshot
  taken at creation (ADR-041 §5), and the profile screen does not reach back into an existing
  document — so a document made by the importer carried a required item satisfiable nowhere in the
  app. Two `<input>`s. Only putting an export gate in front of an imported document reaches this.

- **A `text-primary` link inside a SENTENCE needs an underline; one that is the whole content of its
  element does not.** axe's `link-in-text-block` is `serious` and fires only on the first, which is
  why every other such link in this app passes. `/settings/profile`'s "add one" link arrived in the
  concurrent session's commit and failed the sweep this session added the route to.

- **An edge-case pass over Session 29 found ELEVEN defects, and seven of them were controls that
  could not do anything.** Read ADR-041's second addendum. The mechanical check that found them took
  a minute and is worth running at the end of any session that adds a screen: **sweep the i18n
  catalogue for keys the session added that no source file references.** Thirty-three came back. Nine
  were "Save as my template" (the brief's item 6 — the whole pure layer shipped tested, with no
  dialog); ten were the Ctrl+/ shortcuts sheet; the rest were a letterhead, a `-Sd/-` checkbox, a
  signature-position select, a default copy-to list, a profile nudge and a numeral-conversion
  confirmation. Every one had a label in both languages and did nothing. This is ADR-039's second
  addendum arriving in a new module, and the lesson generalises: **an i18n key with no reader is a
  feature with no reader.**

- **The terminology lint could never fire, and the reason is worth knowing before you write another
  pure checker.** `lintDocument` takes the glossary as an ARGUMENT, because `data/glossary.json` is
  970 KB and a pure function that reaches for a dataset puts the dataset in whatever chunk imports
  the function (ADR-041 §6). That decision is right and it left nobody responsible for handing the
  argument over — so the check was implemented, tested five ways, and returned `[]` on every run.
  If you make a dataset an argument, the same commit owes it a caller.

- **Ask "which slot does this edit" ONCE.** `DocEditorPage` asked twice — the read said
  `bodyHi ? bodyHi : body`, the write said `lang === 'bilingual' ? bodyHi : body` — and for a
  bilingual document with no `bodyHi` (a shape the schema permits) the officer saw the English text,
  typed one character, and the English vanished. `src/lib/drafting/docLang.ts#bodySlotForLanguage` is
  the one answer, and `separateHindiBody` is the affordance that was missing.

- **`String.replace`'s callback has no capture groups when the pattern has none, so `args[2]` is the
  whole input.** Find-and-replace expanded `$2` into the entire paragraph. `$1` escaped only by luck:
  `args[1]` was the offset, a number, which a `typeof` guard rejected by accident. Slice the groups
  out of the tail — `args.slice(1, args.length - 2)`, or `- 3` when named groups add their object.

- **Every document migrated from the Session 8 editor carries a dd.mm.yyyy date, and two places read
  it as ISO.** `Number(date.slice(0, 4))` reads **28** out of `28.09.2026` — and 28 is truthy, so it
  never reached the fallback: issuing a reference number on a migrated document stamped `seqYear: 28`
  and restarted a yearly-reset series. The `<input type="date">` beside it rendered EMPTY for the
  same documents, telling an officer their document had no date when it had one. `parseDate` reads
  both shapes in either script; `yearOfDocument` and `format.ts#isoDateValue` are the two lines that
  were missing between it and the callers.

- **The editor stays editable under the conflict banner, so a write can be in flight when the officer
  answers.** "Take the other tab's version" set the document, cleared the banner, and left the
  debounce armed — 700 ms later the officer's text landed on top of the version they had just chosen.
  `resolveConflict` cancels the pending write first, for both answers.

- **`src/lib/drafting/purity.test.ts` runs its rules over the DIRECTORY and keeps the hand-written
  list as a separate assertion — copy this shape back to `src/lib/srs` and `src/lib/study`.** Those
  two loop over the list, so a file added and not listed is a file no rule applies to until somebody
  notices. Reading the directory means a new file is guarded from the moment it lands; the ledger
  still catches "added without being looked at", it just is not what decides whether the file is
  guarded. This mattered immediately — Session 30 is building the import/export layer in the same
  directory in the same working tree, and its eight files were covered by every rule before either
  session had committed.

- **ADR-041 §2 claimed that purity test existed before it did.** An invariant described rather than
  implemented is what ADR-037's addendum says to distrust on sight, and an ADR is where the next
  session goes to find out what is guaranteed. Writing the file immediately found
  `versions.ts#prune` ordering ISO instants with `localeCompare` — `prune` does not display a list,
  it slices one and its caller deletes what fell off.

- **(Session 29/30's note, kept.) Sessions 29 and 30 ran concurrently in this working tree and coordinated by direct message**, the
  arrangement Sessions 12/13, 14, 15, 21 and the law/pay sessions established. Ownership was split by
  path: Session 30 owns `src/lib/drafting/{html,zip,extract,importDocx,importPdf,paste,letterhead,print,docx}.ts`,
  `src/modules/drafting/{import,print,batch}/**`, `ExportBar.tsx` and Dexie **v15**; this session owns
  v14 and everything else under `src/modules/drafting`. Two things that bit and are worth expecting:
  a peer's in-progress file made `pnpm build` fail, which killed a Playwright run with
  "Process from config.webServer was not able to start" and nothing about the real cause; and my
  purity test's exhaustive file list went red four times while their files landed, which is why it
  now guards by directory and ledgers by name.

- **The MODEL was the deliverable, and `src/lib/drafting/model.ts` is where to start reading.**
  Sessions 30 (print, `.docx`) and 31 (an issue register, threads) build on it, and two members are
  already there waiting for Session 31 with nothing writing them: `linkedIntakeId` and `threadId`,
  the arrangement Dexie v11 made for the Library's annotation tables. `docs/DATA-GAPS.md` #78 is the
  first thing Session 30 should do — `docx.ts` and the print stylesheet still read only `lines`, so a
  table exports as a tab-separated line while the screen shows a real table.

- **One renderer, and it deliberately produces the OLD block shape.** `renderOfficialDoc` returns the
  same `RenderResult` `renderDocument` returns; `RenderedBlock.nodes` is additive and `lines` is
  generated from it. That is what let `pnpm test` stay green with both models live, and it is why
  there is one checklist evaluator rather than two. If you are tempted to give the new model its own
  block type, read ADR-041 §3 first — the cost is a second implementation of `checklist.ts`.

- **`paraNumberingHolds` now reads `nodes` when they are there, and that was forced.** An editor body
  may contain a heading, a list item, a quotation or a table row, and over `lines` alone none of
  those is distinguishable from a paragraph that lost its number — so an appeal with a "Grounds of
  appeal" heading failed a rule it satisfies. Where there are no `nodes` the behaviour is exactly
  what it was, which is every draft of the fourteen original forms.

- **A version diff must ignore the automatic paragraph numbers.** They are generated by POSITION, so
  inserting a paragraph renumbers every line below it — and the first `diffDocuments` reported one
  insertion as a change to the whole rest of the document. Its own test caught it. `linesOf` in
  `versions.ts` strips the marker from a `para` and keeps it on a `listItem`, because a bullet is
  something the officer wrote and a paragraph number is something the renderer counted.

- **A template variable's `sample` is required, and it is not decoration.** The seed DERIVES each
  form's `paras` worked example from its skeleton by substituting these. Without one, a form ships a
  worked example still containing `{{key}}` — and `noPlaceholders` is a `must` on most of the
  library, so the form would fail its own checklist. `tests/drafting-library.test.ts` asserts both
  halves, over all forty-three.

- **`{{#if}}` and `{{#each}}` are whole marker PARAGRAPHS and their field names must be ASCII.**
  `[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9]*`, the same id shape the zod schema, the JSON Schema and the seed's
  self-check all use. A Devanagari name is not an opener at all: it renders as literal text and the
  `{{/if}}` below it becomes a closer with nothing to close. `skeleton.test.ts` asserts exactly that
  rather than leaving it to be discovered, because the failure is the quiet kind — a Hindi skeleton
  written that way prints its own control flow onto an official document.

- **A profile change never rewrites a document, and neither does deleting an addressee.**
  `meta.from`, `meta.signature` and every entry in `meta.to`/`meta.copyTo` are SNAPSHOTS; `bookId` is
  a convenience pointer and nothing renders from it. `deleteAddressee` returns how many documents
  still name the person so the confirmation can say so, and `documents.test.ts` asserts the document
  is untouched — "we did not cascade the delete" is a claim, not a comment.

- **Do not copy `useGlobalShortcuts`'s mount-only-plus-latest-ref shape without asking why it exists.**
  It needs it because it holds state ACROSS keypresses (a pending `g` chord and its timer). The
  editor's Ctrl+S/Ctrl+P/Ctrl+F handler holds none, so it uses an ordinary dependency array — the
  comment at that effect says so. The Library reader learned the same lesson the expensive way
  (ADR-038's addendum).

- **jsdom cannot prove the editor keeps the caret, and the obvious test that claims to is a lie.**
  Asserting the paragraph's DOM node is the same object after a re-render PASSES against a version
  with the `lastEmitted` guard deleted, because ProseMirror diffs the document it is given and reuses
  the nodes. The only thing the guard protects is the SELECTION, and jsdom implements no layout —
  `Range.getClientRects` is absent, and stubbing it makes ProseMirror place typed characters _worse_
  than the absence does. The claim is in `tests/e2e/draft-editor.spec.ts`, and there is a comment
  where the jsdom test would have been saying why it is not there.

- **A marker glyph inside a tab's accessible name is both an a11y defect and a test trap.** The
  Review tab's "something must be fixed" dot is `aria-hidden` with an `sr-only` sentence beside it,
  because "Review bullet" means nothing to a screen reader — and because Playwright matches a string
  `name` as a case-insensitive SUBSTRING, so `{ name: 'Review' }` also matched "Preview". CLAUDE.md
  already recorded that trap costing half an hour on `{ name: 'Post' }` matching "Place of posting".

- **A hint nested inside a `<label>` becomes part of the control's accessible name.** Three fields
  shipped that way and the input's name read "Pattern Tokens: {FILE} {SEQ} {YEAR}…", which made the
  field unfindable by its own name. The hint is a sibling with `aria-describedby` now. A name says
  what the control IS; a description says what to put in it.

- **`--destructive` has no paired foreground for a TINT.** `bg-destructive/10` with
  `text-destructive-foreground` failed `color-contrast` on fourteen elements the first time the
  review panel was swept in a browser. Marigold, tulsi and coral are the three that carry a
  `-foreground` for their own `/15`; an error row is coral. CLAUDE.md recorded the same thing about
  `EraseSection`'s `bg-destructive/5`, which is a hint that this is worth a token rather than a rule
  everyone rediscovers. And `--muted-foreground` fails on those tints too, so a CSMOP reference line
  inside a failing row inherits the row's colour instead.

- **The library went from 14 forms to 43 and `drafting_forms.py` defines no helper of its own.**
  `drafting_seed.py` hands it `field`/`block`/`check`/`template`/`ref` and the shared block
  constants, so there is one definition of what a template is and one `self_check` over all
  forty-three. Adding a form is a `mk(...)` entry plus a line in `src/modules/drafting/data.ts`,
  `scripts/ingest/validate_data.py`'s manifest and the digest in `data/_meta/versions.json` —
  `tests/drafting-data.test.ts` and `tests/drafting-library.test.ts` will tell you which you forgot.

- **What this session did NOT finish, and where each is written down.** The brief's item 11 asked for
  slash commands and an insert-glossary-term/insert-phrase control wired into the editor's toolbar:
  the toolbar carries both buttons and they open the Details tab, because the glossary sheet and the
  phrase sheet are Session 8 components built around a textarea's caret and porting them onto a
  ProseMirror selection is its own piece of work. Slash commands are not there at all — the toolbar
  and Ctrl+S/Ctrl+P/Ctrl+F are. `docs/DATA-GAPS.md` #78 is the bigger one: print and `.docx` still
  read `lines` and not `nodes`, so a table exports flat, and Session 30 owns both.

- **`data/_meta/versions.json` carries a sha256 over the templates and it is hand-maintained.** It is
  the digest of every `data/drafting/templates/*.json` plus `index.json`, concatenated in sorted path
  order. Re-running the seed changes it; `tests/drafting-data.test.ts` fails until it is updated.

- **An edge-case pass over this session found FOURTEEN defects, and the pattern was ADR-039's, not
  ADR-032's.** There IS a model here and its half was guarded — citations re-derived, a personal
  snippet never presented as law, the screen run before the provider is constructed. What failed was
  the code around it, in three families, and ADR-040's addendum has all fourteen. The four most
  transferable are below; every regression test was confirmed to fail against the committed code
  first (`src/lib/retrieval.edge.test.ts`, `src/lib/study/edge.test.ts`,
  `src/modules/library/study.edge.test.tsx`, `src/ai/tools/library.edge.test.ts`).

- **`numberKey` folded `18(2)` into `182`, which is a REAL rule number.** 256 of GFR's 307 rule
  numbers were reachable that way and `1(1)` collides with Rule 11 in every one of the nine books
  with eleven rules. Because the exact-number pass scores 1.0, it put a stranger level with the
  provision the reader asked for. This is **ADR-035's `refKey()` lesson one resolution further down**
  — there a digits-only key could not tell 124 from 124A — and the file already contained a test
  named "keeps 124 and 124A apart" two blocks above the assertion that encoded the new collision.
  A key that throws away structure throws away identity. `PROVISION` separately missed `s 65B`, which
  the session brief names verbatim, and `F.R. 17(1)`, which is what this repo's own `citation()`
  prints.

- **A rail component that is not keyed on the unit will save one provision's writing against
  another.** `j`/`k` navigate without unmounting the rail, so `FeynmanBox` kept the textarea's
  contents across a unit change and `saveAttempt` read `unit.id` from the props it had _now_. Write
  about Rule 3, press `j`, press Save, and it is stored against Rule 4 — nothing throws and both
  screens look correct. `ChapterRevisionCard` and `StudyAskPanel` leaked confirmations the same way.
  Fixed with a `key`, never an effect that clears state (`ReviewPage`'s `wrongAnswer` rule).

- **A surface that records as it goes must not also offer a "save" that records again.** The chapter
  quiz graded every answer through `reviewCard` as it was given, and "add the ones I got wrong to my
  review deck" graded them a second time — cutting FSRS stability from 4.72 days to 1.51 on a matured
  card and writing a `reviewLog` row for a review that never happened. `reviewLog` is what the weekly
  review counts and what retention is measured from, so it outlives the schedule. The screen states
  what is already true and links to the deck instead.

- **Four features were wired end to end and could never fire** — the third session in a row to land
  on this. The coverage heat-map was mounted `cards={null}`, so `quizzed` was false for every unit
  and `readNotQuizzed` was `read` under another name; the Pomodoro lengths had no setter although
  `clampPomodoro` was written, bounded and tested; the Ask panel rendered on a reader-added document
  where every tool refuses a `my-` id, so it could only ever say "it could not answer"; and
  `get_related_cards` loaded twelve rule books to answer about one. Ask what would have to be true
  for a control to succeed, and check that it can be.

- **Two committed tests were asserting the defects.** `retrieval.test.ts` asserted
  `numberKey('318 (4)') === '3184'` and `analytics.test.ts` asserted a streak of 0 for a reader who
  studied yesterday and not yet today — while `src/lib/srs/day.ts#currentStreak`, one directory over,
  had always counted from yesterday, so two screens contradicted each other about one reader every
  morning. ADR-037's `token`-suppression lesson again: when an edge pass contradicts a committed
  assertion, decide which is describing the app.

- **`role="img"` belongs on a `<div>` of `<span>`s, never on a `<ul>`** — and the first test written
  for a `React.lazy` component's ABSENCE cannot fail. `StudyAskPanel` is lazy, so it is missing for a
  tick whatever the gate says; the test now renders a work where the panel _should_ appear first, to
  resolve and cache the module, before asserting it is absent elsewhere. `network.sentinel`'s story
  (ADR-031) in a second place.

- **`Promise.all` in a list nobody is watching is how a feature disappears silently.**
  `useDueChaptersEverywhere` loaded every work with a due chapter that way, so one failed chunk made
  the revise list vanish from both hubs, permanently, with nothing in the console. A due list that
  disappears is worse than a short one — the reader concludes they are up to date. `allSettled` now.

- **The ordering is the deliverable, not the features.** Precomputed first, retrieval always, a model
  last — `docs/AI.md` §13 is the written policy, including why fine-tuning is rejected (grounding is
  retrieval, not weights: a fine-tuned model has no snippets to cite, and `validateCitations()` would
  have to be deleted to accommodate one). When you add a surface, ask in this order: can it be a
  dataset? can it be retrieval over a dataset? can it be a deterministic function over the reader's
  own rows? Only when all three answer no does an agent earn its place — and then it goes at the
  BOTTOM of whatever it is added to, so the surface still works without it.
  `src/modules/library/ai-seam.ts` states the test that keeps this honest.

- **An aid is written once and shipped; nothing about it is generated at read time.** 223 approved
  aids across seven acts, each with the unit's text open, each through the four stages in
  `docs/AUTHORING.md`, each carrying `groundingUnitIds` that resolve. It works offline, on every
  device, with no key, at zero cost, in both languages, and a reader can check where it came from — a
  model cannot beat any of those properties, only be more flexible. `docs/DATA-GAPS.md` #76 has what
  is left: eight works have none, and a second reader over the 223 is real work.

- **`groundingUnitIds` must name units in the aid's OWN work.** The CCA aids first pointed at
  `ccs-conduct-4` and `ccs-conduct-14` — a real and useful comparison — and it silently turned
  `tests/library-aids.test.ts`'s pointer check into a cross-corpus claim, which is a much weaker
  thing to assert. The comparison lives in the aid's `verify.note` prose instead.

- **Reusing an FSRS engine is safe; sharing its TABLE is not.** `src/lib/study/chapters.ts` imports
  `createCard`/`gradeCard` wholesale — they are pure and take a row — and puts the result in
  `chapterCards`. A chapter has no `qId` in `data/rules/cards`, so every catalogue-taking function in
  `src/lib/srs` would look one up and find nothing, and "12 due" on `/study/practise` would mean twelve of two
  different things. `src/lib/study/independence.test.ts` grades one deck `Easy` and the other `Again`
  for the SAME underlying rule, so the claim cannot pass by accident.

- **A purity guard that matches source text needs to strip comments first.**
  `src/lib/study/purity.test.ts` has a `code()` helper because `analytics.ts` type-imports `@/db`
  (erased at compile time, reaches no database) and `quiz.ts` names `Math.random()` in a comment
  explaining why it does not use it. `src/lib/srs/purity.test.ts` avoided both only by choosing a
  pattern its own prose happened not to match — which works until somebody writes the call form in a
  comment. `import type` is excluded deliberately, with the reason written at the exclusion.

- **A two-character query never reaches fuse.js, and an exact heading loses to a glossary entry of
  the same name.** `src/lib/retrieval.ts` runs a NUMBER pass at score 1.0 and an exact-HEADING pass at
  0.98 before fuse for those two reasons; the second was found because "Suspension" returned a
  glossary term whose citation is literally `"Suspension / निलंबन"` ahead of CCA Rule 10, whose
  citation never contains the word. **The fix is not to re-weight `heading` above `citation`** — a
  citation is still the only unambiguous field, and "Definitions" is a heading four rule books share.
  `KIND_ORDER` breaks an exact tie towards the source.

- **`fuse.js`'s `limit` only slices an already fully-scored array, so `limit: k * 4` broke scope
  filtering.** With `k: 1` and a narrow scope, the only in-scope match fell past the multiplier and
  `retrieve` returned nothing. There is no limit now and the loop breaks at `k` in-scope hits.

- **Four of the 40 retrieval fixtures were my own over-claims and were corrected with reasons rather
